subject.title: fix(cron): keep no-channel implicit cron runs successful instead of failing delivery (#56078)

question: Should implicit no-channel announce-to-last cron delivery become ok/not-delivered once proof and docs are supplied, or should this wait for a broader cron warning-status/default-delivery direction?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and internally consistent, but it changes cron status, retry, and operator-alert semantics for existing no-channel runs and overlaps broader cron delivery policy work.

options.title: Require Proof And Docs, Then Accept Narrow Fix
options.body: Ask for redacted installed no-channel agentTurn cron proof and the CLI docs update, then allow this bounded ok/not-delivered mitigation to proceed.

options.title: Override Proof Based On Focused Evidence
options.body: A maintainer may accept the dispatcher, gateway command-cron, and CI evidence as enough while owning the remaining end-to-end user-path proof risk.

options.title: Pause For Broader Status Model
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers want the warning-status/default-delivery work to own the behavior instead.

recommendation.title: Require Proof And Docs, Then Accept Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted installed no-channel agentTurn cron proof and the CLI docs update, then allow this bounded ok/not-delivered mitigation to proceed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history in the cron delivery resolver and dispatch paths that define this semantic boundary.
